issues.legal_issue: A municipal district may be constituted from portions of villages rather than only from whole villages.
material_facts: The government notified a proposed municipal district whose boundaries included portions of several villages.
After considering objections, the government declared the area a municipal district under the statutory provisions governing municipal boundaries.
issues.conclusion: The notifications were not contrary to or beyond the powers conferred by sections 4 and 7; the government could include portions of villages when constituting the municipal district.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 7 of the Bombay District Municipal Act, 1901 permit the government to constitute a municipal district and to alter its limits. Section 7 allows adjoining land to be included, and neither provision restricts the government to including an entire village or suburb.

predicates.municipal_boundary_challenge: The proceeding challenges the constitution or boundaries of a municipal district.
predicates.proposed_area_includes_part_of_village: The government included only part of a village in the proposed municipal district.

issues.definition: When a challenge to municipal boundaries concerns an area that includes part of a village, the inclusion of that part is authorized.

issues.legal_issue: Municipal rules imposing a rate on buildings must state the applicable property class, rate, and basis of valuation, but need not prescribe the particular method for calculating annual letting value.
material_facts: The municipality framed house-tax rules that identified the liable class as buildings or houses.
The rules set the rate and provided for assessment on net annual letting value, without specifying a particular method for calculating that value.
The companies argued that the rules were invalid because they did not prescribe the method of valuation.
issues.conclusion: The rules conformed to the statutory requirements because they specified the property class, rate, and annual letting value as the basis of valuation; they did not also have to prescribe a particular method for arriving at that value.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 59 and 60 of the Bombay District Municipal Act, 1901 govern municipal rates on buildings or lands and the requirements for imposing them. A rate is based on annual value, which may be ascertained by recognized methods, including actual rent, hypothetical rent, or a capital-value method used to derive annual value. The municipality must specify the basis it adopts, but need not specify the method of calculation. Patel Goverdhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad was relied on for the meaning of a rate and the recognized approaches to annual value; Lokmanya Mills v. Barsi Borough Municipality was relied on for the distinction between the valuation basis and a method such as floor-area calculation.

rule.if: municipal_property_rate_rule_challenge and rules_identify_liable_property_class and rules_state_rate and rules_state_annual_value_basis

predicates.municipal_property_rate_rule_challenge: The proceeding challenges rules imposing a municipal rate on buildings or land.
predicates.rules_identify_liable_property_class: The municipality's rules identify the class of property made liable for the rate.
predicates.rules_state_rate: The municipality's rules state the rate applicable to the liable property class.
predicates.rules_state_annual_value_basis: The municipality's rules state annual value as the basis for assessing the rate.

issues.definition: Rules challenged in a municipal property-rate proceeding satisfy the valuation-basis requirement when they identify the liable property class, state the rate, and state annual value as the valuation basis.

issues.legal_issue: A flat rate based on carpet area may be used to assess a building only if it corresponds to the building's annual letting value.
material_facts: The municipality assessed factory buildings using a flat rate based on carpet area.
The governing rules required assessment on annual letting value but did not require one particular method for calculating that value.
The court did not determine whether the carpet-area calculations in these assessments corresponded to annual letting value and left that factual question for the pending appeals.
issues.conclusion: A flat rate based on carpet area is not necessarily impermissible, but the assessment may be challenged if that calculation does not reflect annual letting value; the companies could attempt to establish that in their appeals.
issues.legal_principle: The rules required assessment on annual letting value, which could be determined by a recognized method. A carpet-area calculation could serve as a means of arriving at that value if it corresponded to it, but floor area alone could not replace the required valuation basis. Patel Goverdhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad and Lokmanya Mills v. Barsi Borough Municipality were relied on in explaining annual letting value and the limits on floor-area valuation.

predicates.municipal_building_rate_assessment_chall: The proceeding challenges a municipal rate assessment of buildings.
predicates.flat_carpet_area_method_used: The assessing authority calculated the building assessment using a flat rate based on carpet area.

issues.definition: In a challenge to a building-rate assessment calculated by flat carpet area, that calculation is permissible only if it reflects the building's annual letting value.

issues.legal_issue: Open land cannot be separately assessed as a building or house under rules whose scope is limited to roofed structures.
material_facts: The house-tax rules applied to buildings, houses, shops, or huts and defined a building or house as a structure with a roof, constructed for habitation or otherwise.
The assessment bills separately included open land, and the assessing officer relied on the broader statutory definition of a building rather than the definition in the rules.
The rules provided that expressions defined in the rules would carry the rules' definitions.
issues.conclusion: The assessment of open land was beyond the rules and invalid; open land could not be included while rating the factory buildings under those rules.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 59 and 60 of the Bombay District Municipal Act, 1901 authorize rates on buildings or lands subject to the municipality's rules specifying the liable property class and valuation basis. Rules 1(ii), 3(7), and 3(9) limited these house-tax rules to the stated structures and made the rules' definition of building or house controlling over the broader definition in section 3(7) of the Act. Open land was not within that definition or the rules' scope.

predicates.house_tax_assessment_challenge: The proceeding challenges an assessment made under municipal house-tax rules.
predicates.rules_cover_only_roofed_structures: The applicable rules limit their scope to structures with roofs and do not include open land.
predicates.open_land_separately_assessed: The assessing authority separately assessed open land as taxable property.

issues.definition: A separate assessment of open land is invalid when a house-tax assessment is challenged and the applicable rules cover only roofed structures.
